relation_statement: The attention gate tensor must be sliced to align with each TP rank's query/key/value partition when output_gate is enabled and num_query_groups < tp_size.
observable_signal: slice range/extent of the gate tensor applied on each TP rank versus that rank's query-group partition extent
validity_precondition: self-attention modules with output_gate=True and num_query_groups < tensor_model_parallel_size
evidence_from_issue: MoE/DSA gate not sliced when num_query_groups < tp_size
evidence_from_fix: the gate tensor was not sliced per TP rank; each TP rank multiplied its query/key/value partition by the full unsliced gate, producing wrong attention output but no error

relation_statement: The gradient buffer consumed by the optimizer must be the same buffer written by backward (decoupled_grad) under Megatron-FSDP with a fused optimizer.
observable_signal: parameter values unchanged across optimizer_step despite nonzero decoupled_grad norm
validity_precondition: Megatron-FSDP parameters optimized by FusedAdam with precision-aware optimizer (gradients written to param.decoupled_grad)
evidence_from_issue: FusedAdam.use_decoupled_grad not set for Megatron-FSDP, gradients silently ignored
evidence_from_fix: use_decoupled_grad flag was never set to True, so the optimizer kept reading param.grad (None or stale), silently skipping the actual gradient update

relation_statement: Persistent buffers such as the router expert bias must retain their pre-warmup values after CUDA graph capture warmup.
observable_signal: checksum of the router expert_bias buffer before vs after graph warmup/capture
validity_precondition: MoE router with aux-loss-free routing (expert_bias) when CUDA graph warmup runs the router forward
evidence_from_issue: CUDA-graph warmup overwrites MoE router expert_bias persistent buffer
evidence_from_fix: _CudaGraphRunner saved/restored parameter grads but not persistent buffers; warmup forward passes mutated expert_bias, and post-capture state diverged from pre-capture state

relation_statement: The number of tokens entering each expert must match the router's tokens_per_expert counts when no quantization requires alignment padding.
observable_signal: permuted token buffer length vs sum(tokens_per_expert) (extra zero padding tokens entering experts)
validity_precondition: MoE fused permute path with tokens_per_expert provided on non-quantized models (no FP8/FP4)
evidence_from_issue: MoE permute pads tokens unnecessarily for non-quantized dispatch
evidence_from_fix: get_align_size_for_quantization defaulted to 16 even for non-quantized models, padding tokens to multiples of 16, leading to extra zero tokens entering experts and slightly different expert outputs

relation_statement: Expert parameter buffers used in forward must equal the optimizer's updated main parameters after parameter synchronization completes, even when the gather group size is 1.
observable_signal: expert parameter checksum vs updated main-parameter values after param sync (stale values from previous step's gather buffer)
validity_precondition: layerwise distributed optimizer with expert data-parallel instance size == 1 and MoE expert parameters present
evidence_from_issue: Layerwise distributed optimizer never marks param_gather as dispatched when expt_dp_size=1
evidence_from_fix: param_gather_dispatched remained False so finish_param_sync never executed; expert params were left at uninitialized/stale values from previous step's gather buffer

relation_statement: Zeroing a gradient buffer must leave parameter data of buckets still pending all-gather unchanged when grad and param buffers share storage.
observable_signal: parameter-buffer checksum of pending buckets before vs after grad_data zeroing
validity_precondition: reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag with overlap_param_gather and multiple buckets sharing grad/param storage
evidence_from_issue: mxfp8 reuse_grad_buf zeros wrong buffer (grad_data instead of param_data)
evidence_from_fix: zeroing bucket.grad_data also wiped out param data of other buckets that had not yet completed all-gather, silently corrupting weights

relation_statement: The accumulated weight gradient must equal the sum of per-microbatch gradients written into the live main_grad buffer under FSDP gradient accumulation fusion.
observable_signal: main_grad buffer staleness (data_ptr differs from the per-iteration reconstructed buffer) and accumulated wgrad vs reference sum of microbatch gradients
validity_precondition: Megatron-FSDP parameters (FSDP DTensor) with gradient_accumulation_fusion in linear backward
evidence_from_issue: FSDP grad accumulation fusion missing main_grad creation in linear backward
evidence_from_fix: main_grad must be reconstructed in-place via weight.get_main_grad() each iteration; without this, main_grad pointed to a stale buffer, so accumulated weight gradients were wrong

relation_statement: The per-token loss scale must include the context_parallel_size factor so the effective gradient matches the CP=1 reference.
observable_signal: gradient magnitude ratio between CP>1 and CP=1 runs (off by 1/cp_size)
validity_precondition: calculate_per_token_loss=True in loss function and pipeline forward_step
evidence_from_issue: calculate_per_token_loss with CP misses context_parallel_size scale factor
evidence_from_fix: with per-token loss the CP factor was missing, so when CP later divided again the resulting gradient was off by 1/cp_size

relation_statement: An encoder rank receiving gradients from multiple decoder TP ranks must average (not sum) them so the boundary gradient is not scaled by the TP fanout factor.
observable_signal: encoder-side received gradient norm vs mean of decoder-side sent gradients (inflated by the TP-fanout factor)
topology_scope: PP>1 with encoder TP < decoder TP
validity_precondition: encoder-decoder pipeline boundary where one encoder TP rank receives gradients from multiple decoder TP ranks
evidence_from_issue: encoder->decoder PP gradients summed instead of averaged when ETP < DTP
evidence_from_fix: _handle_tensor_list reduced via torch.stack(...).sum(dim=0); the fix is mean(dim=0): summing scaled the encoder gradient by the TP-fanout factor

relation_statement: Replicated router/gate weights must be identical across DP ranks after module construction, even when perform_initialization=False.
observable_signal: cross-DP-rank checksum of the router weight after module creation
validity_precondition: MoE router or shared-expert gate creation with config.perform_initialization=False (weights expected to be loaded from checkpoint)
evidence_from_issue: MoE router weight initialized with DP RNG fork even when perform_initialization=False
evidence_from_fix: the else branch also unconditionally re-initialized the weight on CPU outside any RNG fork, silently re-randomizing router weights with different values across DP ranks

relation_statement: The router expert-bias buffer must preserve its full-precision (fp32) dtype under mixed-precision module wrapping.
observable_signal: expert_bias.dtype observed as bf16 instead of fp32 at runtime
validity_precondition: Float16Module-wrapped model with MoE TopKRouter using aux-loss-free expert_bias under bf16/fp16 training
evidence_from_issue: MoE expert_bias silently downcast to bf16 by Float16Module wrapper
evidence_from_fix: the expert_bias buffer was demoted to bf16; subsequent in-place updates accumulated in bf16, losing precision and silently distorting routing decisions

relation_statement: The layer-to-pipeline-stage assignment computed by the hybrid model stack must equal the global transformer layer offset map under uneven first/last stage configurations.
observable_signal: per-rank layer offset from the Mamba stack vs get_transformer_layer_offset (mismatched layer types/weights vs checkpoint)
validity_precondition: hybrid Mamba models with num_layers_in_first/last_pipeline_stage set (uneven layer distribution across PP stages)
evidence_from_issue: Mamba hybrid PP layer selection ignores uneven first/last stage configuration
evidence_from_fix: offset = pp_rank * (num_layers // pp_size) assumed even partitioning; MambaStack disagreed with TransformerLayer.get_transformer_layer_offset, silently mismatching layer types/weights vs. checkpoints

relation_statement: The fp32 residual stream must preserve its dtype through bias-dropout-add rather than being downcast to the bf16 branch dtype.
observable_signal: output dtype of the bias-dropout-add result (bf16 instead of fp32) when the residual is fp32
validity_precondition: fp32 residual connection combined with a bf16 compute branch in bias-dropout-add
evidence_from_issue: fp32 residual connection silently downcast to bf16
evidence_from_fix: _bias_dropout_add_func downcasts residual to x.dtype (bf16) instead of upcasting x to residual.dtype (fp32)

relation_statement: The input gradient produced by a frozen-weight TP linear must be all-reduced so all TP ranks pass the identical summed dgrad to upstream layers.
observable_signal: cross-TP-rank difference of grad_input leaving the frozen-weight linear backward
validity_precondition: column/row-parallel linear with frozen weights (requires_grad=False) on the asynchronous all-reduce path
evidence_from_issue: LinearWithFrozenWeight backward skips TP all-reduce of dgrad when TP>1
evidence_from_fix: backward computed grad_input without the cross-TP all-reduce; downstream layers received TP-rank-local input gradients instead of the summed gradient

relation_statement: Input jitter must be applied to the router input before gating, not to the logits after gating, whenever input jitter is enabled in training.
observable_signal: none_runtime: the jitter insertion point is a code-order property; its downstream effect on z-loss gradient direction is statistical rather than a crisp runtime predicate
validity_precondition: MoE TopKRouter with moe_input_jitter_eps > 0 and training=True
evidence_from_issue: MoE input jitter applied AFTER gating instead of before, jittering gradients not inputs
evidence_from_fix: routing called apply_input_jitter(logits) AFTER computing logits; jittering logits changes Z-loss reference and z-loss gradient direction, silently degrading load balancing

relation_statement: The realized token-to-expert dispatch mapping must preserve the router's top-k (token, expert_slot) assignment layout on every EP rank.
observable_signal: dispatched local (token, expert) pairs vs a reference mapping recomputed from the routing indices (masked_select flat ordering)
validity_precondition: MoE base-layer dispatch path with moe_router_topk > 1
evidence_from_issue: MoE local_indices wrong via fancy indexing on bool mask when topk > 1
evidence_from_fix: advanced indexing collapses dimensions breaking the (token, expert_slot) layout, resulting in tokens being routed to the wrong experts on each EP rank

relation_statement: MoE expert outputs must be invariant to the TP degree, which requires gathering tokens across TP ranks even when sequence_parallel=False and EP=1.
observable_signal: expert input token count on each TP rank vs the full gathered token count (each rank processes only its local slice)
validity_precondition: MoE with GroupedGEMM experts and sequence_parallel=False
evidence_from_issue: MoE GroupedGEMM produces wrong outputs without sequence_parallel even when TP>1
evidence_from_fix: with TP>1 but SP=False (and EP=1) neither predicate was True, so expert tokens were never gathered across TP ranks and each TP rank produced wrong (incomplete) MoE outputs

relation_statement: The logged auxiliary (MTP) loss must accumulate contributions from every iteration within the logging window rather than keeping only the last iteration's value.
observable_signal: logged MTP loss vs recomputed average of per-iteration losses over the log_interval window
validity_precondition: Multi-Token Prediction enabled with log_interval > 1
evidence_from_issue: MTP per-layer loss overwritten instead of accumulated when log_interval > 1
evidence_from_fix: save_loss_to_tracker assigned total_loss_dict[name] = loss regardless of whether the key existed; only the most recent iteration's MTP loss survived instead of the average over log_interval steps

relation_statement: The gradient accumulation buffer must be zero at the start of accumulation so the accumulated gradient equals the sum of microbatch gradients only.
observable_signal: nonzero main_grad buffer content (leftover main parameter values) before the first backward accumulation
validity_precondition: first training iteration after init/checkpoint with reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag and overlap_param_gather, before the forward_pre_hook is registered
evidence_from_issue: MXFP8 reuse_grad_buf pollutes main grads on first iter when forward_pre_hook is disabled
evidence_from_fix: copying main params into the shared param/grad buffer left main param values inside main_grad, silently turning the next gradient accumulation into 'main_grad += new_grad' with non-zero start state

relation_statement: The attention softmax scale must equal the YaRN mscale formula evaluated with mscale_all_dim under multi-latent attention when the two config fields differ.
observable_signal: computed softmax_scale value vs the config-derived expected value (off by an mscale_all_dim/mscale ratio)
validity_precondition: multi-latent attention with YaRN rotary_scaling_factor != 1.0 and mscale != mscale_all_dim
evidence_from_issue: MLA softmax_scale built from wrong mscale config field
evidence_from_fix: computed softmax_scale from self.config.mscale instead of self.config.mscale_all_dim, producing attention softmax scaling wrong by an mscale_all_dim/mscale ratio, silently distorting attention probabilities

relation_statement: The shared cached loss mask must remain unchanged across samples; per-sample in-place padding modifications must operate on a private copy.
observable_signal: checksum of the cached loss mask across successive dataset __getitem__ calls (mutates after the first padded sample)
validity_precondition: cached-mask branch (create_attention_mask=False) with padded sequences over multiple steps of the same dataset
evidence_from_issue: GPTDataset returns aliased cached_loss_mask; downstream in-place padding mutates the shared cache and corrupts later samples
evidence_from_fix: loss_mask was returned by reference instead of a clone; the first sample with padding silently mutates the shared cache, so every subsequent sample starts from a polluted mask

relation_statement: Each gradient element must be scaled by exactly 1/dp_size once (per its own bucket), not once per bucket over the whole buffer, during gradient reduce preprocessing.
observable_signal: gradient magnitude after preprocessing vs expected 1/dp_size scaling (cumulative (1/dp_size)^num_buckets on affected ranges)
validity_precondition: Megatron-FSDP with multiple buckets per gradient buffer and gradient scaling factor != 1.0
evidence_from_issue: GradReducePipeline scales gbuf.data instead of bucket.data, applying gradient scaling to the wrong tensor span
evidence_from_fix: preprocessing divided every byte of the joint gradient buffer once per bucket, yielding cumulative scaling of (1/dp_size)**num_buckets instead of (1/dp_size), with no shape mismatch

relation_statement: The gradient scaling factor must equal 1/(dp_size*cp_size), matching the span of the gradient reduction collective, when context parallelism is enabled.
observable_signal: effective gradient magnitude over-scaled by cp_size relative to a CP=1 reference
validity_precondition: sample-mean loss (calculate_per_token_loss=False) with DistributedOptimizer or average_in_collective enabled
evidence_from_issue: target_gradient_scaling_factor uses get_data_parallel_world_size without context_parallel, so gradients are over-scaled by cp_size
evidence_from_fix: the gradient reduction collective spans the dp*cp ranks, so gradients should be divided by dp_size*cp_size; only dividing by dp_size leaves a residual factor of cp_size in the parameter updates

relation_statement: The auxiliary (indexer) loss scale must include the 1/num_microbatches divisor so its gradient contribution is weighted consistently with the main loss.
observable_signal: auxiliary-loss gradient contribution ratio vs the main loss (num_microbatches times larger)
validity_precondition: DSA attention variant with num_microbatches > 1 (gradient accumulation) and calculate_per_token_loss=False
evidence_from_issue: DSA indexer loss is not divided by num_microbatches, so the auxiliary loss gradient is overweighted by a factor of num_microbatches
evidence_from_fix: DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler was never given a per-microbatch divisor; the indexer auxiliary loss accumulates num_microbatches times into the gradient instead of being averaged

relation_statement: Each microbatch's expert weight gradient must be accumulated exactly once; the wgrad accumulate-and-reduce hooks must fire on the modules owning the parameters so param.grad is cleared.
observable_signal: residual param.grad after the hooks should have cleared it; expert wgrad norm doubled relative to a single-count reference on subsequent iterations
validity_precondition: grouped-linear fused-ops path with DDP overlap_grad_reduce (wgrad hooks) and multiple microbatches in MoE training
evidence_from_issue: fused-ops backward_dw skips wgrad hooks on the original linear modules, so DDP never zeros param.grad and AccumulateGrad double-counts
evidence_from_fix: hooks were registered on the original fc1/fc2 modules but backward_dw ran on new instances; hooks never fired, param.grad was not cleared, and AccumulateGrad added again into main_grad, silently double-counting expert weight gradients

relation_statement: The gathered activation tensor passed to the fused wgrad GEMM must be contiguous in memory under sequence-parallel TP with gradient accumulation fusion.
observable_signal: all_gathered_input.is_contiguous() flag at fused wgrad kernel entry
validity_precondition: sequence parallel with gradient_accumulation_fusion and upstream reshape/transpose chains that can produce strided tensors
evidence_from_issue: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute does not enforce all_gathered_input.contiguous(), so wgrad GEMM reads a non-contiguous strided tensor as if it were contiguous
evidence_from_fix: the fused kernel indexes the buffer via flat data_ptr arithmetic; it reads the wrong elements while tensor metadata looks valid, so wgrad accumulation produces silently incorrect numbers

relation_statement: The MoE auxiliary loss must be scaled by num_tokens under per-token loss mode so its weight stays consistent with the main loss normalization.
observable_signal: auxiliary-loss contribution relative to the main loss under per-token mode vs the sample-mean reference
validity_precondition: MoE auxiliary load-balancing loss with calculate_per_token_loss enabled
evidence_from_issue: MoE aux loss not scaled by num_tokens in per_token_loss mode
evidence_from_fix: root_cause not provided in the case record

relation_statement: Module outputs under CUDA-graph replay must equal the eager execution reference when activation recompute (checkpointing) is enabled for the same module.
observable_signal: output divergence between graph replay and an eager reference execution of the captured module
validity_precondition: activation recompute via tensor_parallel.checkpoint combined with CUDA graph capture of the same module (warmup or capture phase active)
evidence_from_issue: tensor_parallel.checkpoint runs CheckpointFunction during CUDA graph warmup, causing graph capture to record stale recomputed activations
evidence_from_fix: recomputing the saved forward inside the graph context corrupts the captured graph because random states and saved tensors get rewritten between warmup and capture; on replay the graph produces values that do not match the eager reference

relation_statement: A captured parameter-cast graph for one virtual pipeline stage must write only its own stage's parameter buffer, leaving other stages' buffers unchanged.
observable_signal: parameter-buffer checksum of other virtual-pipeline stages before vs after cast-graph replay
validity_precondition: DDP enable_cuda_graph with multiple VPP stages on the same device sharing a single mempool
evidence_from_issue: DDP cast cudagraph manager runs warmup steps and shares mempool across virtual pipeline stages, corrupting captured param-cast outputs across VPP
evidence_from_fix: multiple VPP stages shared mempool and warmup buffers, so the captured cast graph for one VPP stage could write into another stage's parameter buffer

relation_statement: Optimizer parameter shard views must be detached from autograd (carry no grad_fn) so FP32 parameter gradients are not double-counted.
observable_signal: grad_fn present on the FP32 shard view; doubled gradient contribution for FP32 parameters relative to the FP16/BF16 path
validity_precondition: DistributedOptimizer with FP32 master parameters (e.g. embeddings, layernorm) under mixed-precision training
evidence_from_issue: DistributedOptimizer FP32 shard_model_param uses non-detached view, so the parameter shard participates in autograd and accumulates spurious grad_fn
evidence_from_fix: the FP32 view kept grad_fn alive; an extra grad chain was created, leading to silently doubled gradient contributions for FP32 parameters, inconsistent with the FP16/BF16 path

relation_statement: The bucket-local parameter index map must equal the globally padded parameter index map so optimizer read/write slices align with where the gradients live.
observable_signal: offset mismatch between the bucket-local param_to_index and the global param_index_map for params whose numel is not a multiple of dp_world_size
validity_precondition: DistributedOptimizer with per-param padding/alignment and buckets containing multiple params, at least one with numel not a multiple of data_parallel_world_size
evidence_from_issue: _ParamAndGradBucket builds local param_to_index from naive concatenation, ignoring per-param padding so optimizer reads from misaligned offsets
evidence_from_fix: param_to_index walked params with offset += param.numel() while the global param_index_map already had padded offsets; the optimizer wrote/read different slices than where the gradients lived
